newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-C-C Amatil sees 1997 sales growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-C-C Amatil sees 1997 sales growth.

text.p: Australian-based soft drink group Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd said on Friday it expected to boost sales volumes in calender 1997 as it continued an aggressive growth strategy and A$800 million annual investment programme.
The company earlier reported a small increase in net profit for calendar 1996 to A$142.1 million from A$138.6 million in 1995.

The result was struck on a 24.8 percent increase in sales to A$3.7 billion but was widely expected after the bottler warned the market in November that earlier predictions of a "mid-teens" net profit improvement would not be met.
C-C Amatil, the world's second largest Coca-Cola bottler, said its growth strategy had lifted sales volume and market share, but had hit profits, particularly in Europe.
Managing director Norb Cole said the company would continue its investment programme in 1997, spending around A$800 million, but would focus more on consolidation.
C-C Amatil had no plans to enter new territories during the year, he said, but would invest in all 17 countries in which it currently operates in Asia-Pacific and Europe.
